_comment: pool filename -> display title. Display metadata only: the pool filename stem is the runtime identity key used for saved-selection restore and bonus-round reservation, so a title is NEVER a rename. Order here is meaningless.
_missingReason: Every pool file now has a title, so `_missing` is empty; this key is kept only to record why it was ever non-empty and to retract a claim made here while it was. The former twelve gaps came from two rips whose filenames are bare numbers (NN.flac), which carry no title. The text in this place used to assert that the numeric suffix of tem_NN / spa_NN IS the published track number on the source album. That was FALSE: the gamerip order is DVD-Video audio-track order, not the OST tracklist order -- Intimidation, track 1 of the Tempest 3000 OST, is `52_tem_13.dsp` -- so a tem_NN / spa_NN suffix carries no published track number and must not be read as one. The Space Giraffe titles are publisher-issued; the Tempest 3000 titles are community-sourced and are recorded under `_unverified`.

_unverified.note: Space Giraffe (37_spa_02 / 38_spa_03 / 39_spa_04, plus the album's slot 0): PUBLISHER-ISSUED titles, HIGH confidence. Source: the official Llamasoft soundtrack page (minotaurproject.co.uk/SpaceGiraffe/soundtrack.php) and the official SpaceGiraffeOST.zip hosted there; VGMdb lists it as a commercial digital release (vgmdb.net/album/16832). Audio identity between the repo gamerip and the OST was established by waveform normalized cross-correlation against the reference audio (research pass, 2026-10-11); gamerip order matches the official order 1:1 and durations agree within 0.3 s (the durations compared were the four gamerip files as originally shipped; slot 0 has since been deduped, see the next note). Published credits: Flossie's Frolic = Jeff Minter (credited 'Yak'), Satipn = Redpoint, Side of the Angels = Jim McCauley, Gardening By Numbers = Redpoint. Apostrophe: 'Flossie's Frolic' is written with a straight U+0027, NOT the U+2019 kept in 'Mind’s Eye'. U+2019 is preserved there because the Tempest 2000 rip FILENAME literally contains it, which is the published spelling; the only rip evidence here ('TxK/Flossies Frolic.flac') has no apostrophe at all, and the official page could not be re-fetched from this machine to confirm a typographic one, so the plain ASCII apostrophe is used rather than inventing a typographic spelling. The album's slot 0 (Space Giraffe track 1, 'Flossie's Frolic') is no longer a spa_NN file: the Space Giraffe gamerip copy was retired as a duplicate and slot 0 now aliases 13_flossiesfrolic.dsp -- see the dedupe note. The three remaining spa_NN files are the gamerip copies of OST tracks 2-4, and gamerip order still matches the official order 1:1 for them.

ONE FILE, TWO ALBUMS -- the Space Giraffe copy of this recording was RETIRED as a duplicate (dedupe 2026-10-11, same precedent as the Tempest 3000 re-rips: same-index alias in the manifest, regenerate the maps, prune both pools). The surviving file is this one, 13_flossiesfrolic.dsp (TxK rip, 293.17 s, 5,360,960 B). The retired file was the Space Giraffe gamerip of the same OST track 1 -- slot 0 of the spa_NN set, source soundtracks/Space_Giraffe/01.flac, 596.51 s, 10,907,788 B -- and it is named here by slot, duration and byte size rather than by filename on purpose: a retired pool file should not survive as a grep-able reference. The two were the SAME recording, measured on this machine by lag-searching cross-correlation on the pool .dsp files themselves: every excerpt of the short file matches at lag ~0 AND at lag ~293.28 s with near-identical ncc (0.9495 / 0.9494), and the long file self-correlates at ncc 0.9955 with a seam click at 293.257 s -- i.e. the long file is pass + pass + a 10.06 s closing reprise of the opening. An earlier window study on the FLAC sources agreed: every 5 s window of the 293 s TxK file matches Space_Giraffe/01.flac at ncc 0.964-0.997 (median 0.989) at a single lag drifting 218 -> 269 samples across 293 s, the signature of one master resampled to two rates (31999 Hz gamerip vs 48000 Hz TxK rip), not of two recordings. Space Giraffe slot 0 now aliases this file AT THE SAME INDEX, which is what preserves the album's level bands: 4 unreserved tracks -> bands 0-24 / 25-49 / 50-74 / 75-99 before AND after, and album track changes are level-driven, not duration-driven, so the 293 s file simply loops twice per former period. That is safe because the engine ignores DSP header loop points entirely (loop_flag is 0, loop points span the whole file) and loops by reopening the file at EOF -- music_core.cpp ensureDspData. ACCEPTED LOSS: the 10.06 s closing reprise is not in the TxK file and is therefore gone from the album; the user accepted it, and the source FLAC stays on disk so the decision is reversible. Neither file is named by bonus_rounds. The display title is now the plain official Llamasoft OST name 'Flossie's Frolic' -- the '(TxK)' qualifier this file used to carry was there to tell two pool copies apart, and with one file serving the TxK, Tempest 4000 and Space Giraffe albums it would mislabel the Space Giraffe row. Pool stems are untouched, so saved-selection restore and bonus-round reservation do not move.
_unverified.confidence: high (measured on this machine: lag-searched cross-correlation of the pool .dsp files, plus the earlier FLAC window study)

_unverified.note: Tempest 3000 (46_tem_07 / 47_tem_08 / 52_tem_13 / 54_tem_15 / 56_tem_17): NO publisher-issued tracklist exists anywhere -- nothing on VGMdb, Discogs or Rate Your Music. The only listing is the Nuon-Dome community archive (nuon-dome.com/media.html), which has hosted these soundtrack MP3s with names and credits since ~2001, corroborated by independent YouTube OGST uploads. Composers are T(NT), Andre Meyer and James Grunke -- NOT Jeff Minter. AUDIO identity is proven by waveform normalized cross-correlation against the reference audio; the NAMES are community-sourced, so confidence is bounded by the archive, not by a publisher. Per-file ncc from the research pass (2026-10-11): Crowning Glory (T(NT)) 0.98, Bibble (T(NT)) 0.96, Sht Overload (T(NT)) 0.97, Intimidation (T(NT)) 0.77 with duration 316.2 s vs 317.4 s, and Flash (Andre Meyer) 0.49 -- the weakest of the set (best match by ~5x, but the one most likely to be mislabelled). If a publisher tracklist ever surfaces, Flash and Intimidation are the two to re-check first.
_unverified.confidence: medium (community archive; no publisher tracklist exists)

_unverified.note: 41_tem_02.dsp and 42_tem_03.dsp are NOT Tempest 3000 compositions: both are re-rips of the Tempest 2000 'Thermal Resolution' already in the pool as 00_thermalresolution.dsp. Measured on this machine 2026-10-11: tempest3000_soundtrack/02.flac (133 s) matches T2000 'Thermal Resolution' from +2.16 s at ncc 0.87-0.99 (median 0.97) and tempest3000_soundtrack/03.flac (103 s) matches it from +135.85 s at ncc 0.84-1.00 (median 0.97), each at a constant lag -- i.e. the DVD-Video rip split the one Tempest 2000 track across two audio tracks. They are titled 'Thermal Resolution (T3 edit)' and 'Thermal Resolution (T3 edit 2)' so they cannot collide with the existing 'Thermal Resolution' or 'Thermal Resolution (MOD)' entries in a flat list; both parentheticals are ours, not published, and '(T3 edit 2)' is a numbering of our own making. HAND DIVERGENCE, deliberate: neither title is derived (the tem_NN rip names are bare numbers and carry no title), so these two are hand-authored end to end. The parenthetical used to read '(T3000 Edit)' / '(T3000 Edit 2)'; it was shortened to '(T3 edit)' / '(T3 edit 2)' on 2026-10-11 because the 34- and 36-byte album rows '02 Thermal Resolution (T3000 Edit)' / '03 ... Edit 2)' were the two longest strings the touch panel had to fit and they clipped in the now-playing header and the flat list. T3 is this tree's abbreviation for Tempest 3000 (see music_core.cpp's album comments) and 'edit' is kept because it is the load-bearing word: these are NOT Tempest 3000 compositions, they are edits of the Tempest 2000 track. The pool stems 41_tem_02 / 42_tem_03 are untouched, so saved-selection restore and the bonus-round reservation do not move.
_unverified.confidence: high for the audio identity (measured), ours for the parenthetical suffix

_unverified.note: 'B2' and 'B3' were never titles. They are the bare side labels of the PS Vita gamerip filenames TxK/B2.flac and TxK/B3.flac, which the pool stems 24_b2 / 25_b3 repeat, and both entries used to be recorded here as unnamed placeholders derived from the rip filename. They now carry their published OST titles. SOURCE: 'TxK - The Original Soundtrack', Llamasoft Moosicians, released 2014-02-15, https://txk-ost.bandcamp.com/album/txk-the-original-soundtrack (18 tracks; re-read from the live page 2026-10-12). 24_b2.dsp = OST track 12, 'Coupler - Limaverse', listed 09:04 = 544 s; our file is 544.252 s, delta +0.252 s. 25_b3.dsp = OST track 11, 'Coupler - Limaworld', listed 06:30 = 390 s; our file is 390.000 s, delta 0.000 s (exact). Composer credit is Coupler for both. THE MATCH IS UNIQUE, NOT MERELY CLOSE: no other track on the album falls in 380-400 s or 535-555 s, so each file's duration selects exactly one OST track. THESE ARE TWO DIFFERENT TRACKS AND MUST NOT BE CONFLATED: Limaworld and Limaverse are ADJACENT on the OST (11 then 12) and share one artist, which is precisely the shape that invites a swap -- and the gamerip filename order is REVERSED against the OST order, B2 being OST track 12 and B3 being OST track 11. The 154 s gap between 390 s and 544 s is three orders of magnitude larger than the worst rip-vs-OST duration error here (0.252 s), so duration separates them unambiguously and the pairing above is pinned by the measured numbers, not by the filename. THE ARBITER IF THIS IS EVER DOUBTED: the 544 s file is Limaverse and the 390 s file is Limaworld; check the durations before believing the stems. NO CROSS-ALBUM ARBITRATION IS NEEDED for 24_b2.dsp: it is the one recording shared between our TxK and Tempest 4000 albums (declared in album_aliases.json against tempest4000_soundtrack/29 Limaverse.flac, 544.369 s) and the TxK OST uses the SAME name as the Tempest 4000 release, so both albums display 'Limaverse' for it and nothing has to be chosen between them. HAND DIVERGENCE, deliberate: the derivation reads the rip filename and still derives 'B2' / 'B3', so --write reports a CONFLICT for both files and the hand values win -- see the expected CONFLICT list in gen_track_titles.py. The pool stems 24_b2 / 25_b3 are untouched: stems are the runtime identity key for saved-selection restore and bonus-round reservation, so a title is never a rename. THE OTHER THREE OST DISAGREEMENTS ARE NOW CLOSED, NOT STILL PENDING: this note used to end by recording that the OST also disagreed with three other TxK titles in the pool ('Ginswigger' vs OST track 6 'Gin Swigger', 'Consciousness' vs track 8 'Consciousness Is Feedback', 'Wandering Halls' vs track 18 'Wandering The Halls') and left them as a separate pending decision. That decision was taken on 2026-10-12 and all three now carry their OST titles -- see the note that follows this one for the evidence, including the two of them whose durations do NOT agree with the OST. Scope note for the sentence above about 'the worst rip-vs-OST duration error here (0.252 s)': 'here' means this b2/b3 pair. It is not a tree-wide claim, and it must not be read as one -- the largest game-vs-OST duration gap in the tree is +105.482 s on 32_wanderinghalls.dsp.
_unverified.confidence: high (publisher-issued OST release; unique duration match on both files, +0.252 s and 0.000 s)

_unverified.note: TXK OST TITLE CORRECTIONS, three files, applied 2026-10-12. SOURCE: 'TxK - The Original Soundtrack', Llamasoft Moosicians, Wales UK, released 2014-02-15, 18 tracks, https://txk-ost.bandcamp.com/album/txk-the-original-soundtrack (re-read from the live page 2026-10-12). These three pool titles disagreed with the OST and now match it: 12_consciousness.dsp 'Consciousness' -> OST track 8, 'Spydabee - Consciousness Is Feedback', listed 04:01 = 241 s; 20_ginswigger.dsp 'Ginswigger' -> OST track 6, 'Barry Island - Gin Swigger', listed 03:17 = 197 s; 32_wanderinghalls.dsp 'Wandering Halls' -> OST track 18, 'Governmentyard - Wandering The Halls', listed 04:09 = 249 s. Durations are from track_map.json. DURATION EVIDENCE, all measured: 12_consciousness.dsp = 240.739 s, delta -0.261 s vs t8 -- CLEAN MATCH. 20_ginswigger.dsp = 166.139 s, delta -30.861 s vs t6. 32_wanderinghalls.dsp = 354.482 s, delta +105.482 s vs t18. THE TWO LARGE GAPS WERE CHECKED FOR A BETTER CANDIDATE AND NONE EXISTS: no OST track lies within +/-3 s of 166.139 s (nearest is t3 'Laser Everywhere' at 28.861 s, and t3 is already claimed by 16_lasereverywhere.dsp at delta 0.000 s), and no OST track lies within +/-3 s of 354.482 s (nearest is t13 'Minter Trance' at 13.482 s, itself already claimed by 26_mintertrance.dsp, which is +15.712 s off). The OST's 249 s slot has no candidate in the pool at all. So for both files the gap is a game-edit-vs-album-master length difference, not a misidentification: no alternative OST identity fits better than the one adopted. CAVEAT, STATED HONESTLY: the +105.482 s gap on 32_wanderinghalls.dsp is the largest game-vs-OST gap in the tree and no repo metadata explains it. The rename therefore rests on NAME evidence plus the absence of any better candidate, NOT on duration agreement, and only audio cross-correlation against the album master could confirm the identity outright. That correlation has NOT been measured on this machine (the album master audio is not on it) and remains the outstanding check on this one file. PRECEDENT THAT MAKES LARGE GAME-VS-MASTER GAPS NORMAL HERE: 13_flossiesfrolic.dsp (293.17 s) against the Space Giraffe gamerip of the SAME recording (596.51 s) is a +303 s game-vs-master difference, and it is PROVEN the same recording by cross-correlation (ncc 0.9495 at lag ~0 and ~293.28 s) -- see the dedupe note above. Loop regions cannot explain any duration difference either: track_map.json carries NO loop/segment metadata, and the engine ignores DSP header loop points entirely (loop_flag is 0, loop points span the whole file) and loops by reopening the file at EOF -- music_core.cpp ensureDspData. MISALIGNMENT TEST THAT LICENSES THE WHOLE MAPPING: of the 14 TxK pool files with an OST namesake, 8 match within +/-3 s and 6 do not -- inthezone +3.075, tranceone +3.977, nebulalost -7.935, mintertrance +15.712, ginswigger -30.861, wanderinghalls +105.482 -- which is a continuum, not two outliers. The accounting is nevertheless complete: 17 of the 18 OST tracks are present in the pool (14 by name, plus Limaverse and Limaworld by duration, plus 31_mooing.dsp = t2 'You Like' by the documented dedupe identity at album_aliases.json:211, which retired TxK/youlikeit Final.flac as a duplicate of TxK/mooing.flac), and only t9 "1993 ('92 Mix)" is absent; the 3 non-OST pool files are 13_flossiesfrolic (Space Giraffe), 21_musicarena (Tempest 4000) and 29_hypertest2 (game asset). 17+1=18 and 17+3=20. Wholesale tracklist misalignment is therefore REFUTED, which is what makes a name-based rename safe for the two files whose durations do not agree. GIN SWIGGER SOURCE ARBITRATION, recorded as a decision and not a silent edit: our one-word 'Ginswigger' came from the Tempest 4000 rip filename soundtracks/tempest4000_soundtrack/22 Ginswigger.flac (cited in the TXK_TITLES comment in soundtracks/gen_track_titles.py -- line 215 as of this edit, and a bare line number there drifts whenever the docstring is edited, so anchor on the comment text, not the number); the TxK OST publishes two words. The OST was chosen, by user decision on 2026-10-12. Note that 20_ginswigger.dsp is SHARED between both albums (albums_manifest.json:56 Tempest 4000 slot 16 and :83 TxK index 14, bound at album_aliases.json:169), so ONE display title serves both albums and the spelling being overridden here is the Tempest 4000 rip's. HAND DIVERGENCE, deliberate: the derivation still derives 'Consciousness' (from TxK/Consciousness Final.flac once the ' Final' rip artifact is dropped) and still derives 'Ginswigger' and 'Wandering Halls' via TXK_TITLES, which is left exactly as it is on purpose -- the hand value is meant to win and --write is meant to report a CONFLICT for precisely this reason. See the expected CONFLICT list in gen_track_titles.py. The pool stems 12_consciousness / 20_ginswigger / 32_wanderinghalls are untouched: stems are the runtime identity key for saved-selection restore and bonus-round reservation, so a title is never a rename.
